sequence.title: Purpose and users of financial reporting

syllabus.outcomeReferences: category-level draft; cross-check exact lettering against selected sitting

prerequisites: Basic double entry and primary financial statements
objectives: Explain the objective of general purpose financial reporting.
Distinguish primary users and their information needs.
Separate stewardship, decision usefulness and entity-specific management information.
Apply materiality to a reporting judgement.

workedExample.scenario: A lender asks for a private weekly cash forecast while investors receive annual financial statements.
steps: Explain why a private forecast is entity-specific management/lender information.
Assess whether a covenant uncertainty is material to the annual statements.
workedExample.answer: The annual statements serve existing and potential investors, lenders and other creditors generally. The private weekly forecast is not itself a general-purpose statement. A covenant uncertainty may require recognition, presentation or disclosure analysis if it could influence users' decisions.

practice.answer: Existing and potential investors, lenders and other creditors.
practice.explanation: They cannot normally demand tailored reports.
Materiality depends on nature and magnitude in the entity's circumstances.

practice.answer: It helps users assess management's use of resources.

examTask.prompt: Explain whether omission of a small related-party transaction can be material and identify the relevant reasoning.
modelPoints: Nature can matter even when amount is small.
Conclude from supplied facts, not a universal threshold.

sequence.title: Qualitative characteristics and the cost constraint

syllabus.outcomeReferences: category-level draft; cross-check exact lettering against selected sitting

prerequisites: ACCA FR A1 or equivalent diagnostic
objectives: Distinguish relevance from faithful representation.
Apply comparability, verifiability, timeliness and understandability.
Explain prudence and neutrality without deliberate bias.
Resolve a trade-off using the cost constraint.

workedExample.scenario: Two valuation methods are available: Method X is timely and independently observable but omits a material condition; Method Y includes the condition using a transparent estimate.
steps: Test completeness, neutrality and freedom from error in process.
workedExample.answer: Method X is verifiable but not faithfully representative if it omits a material condition. Method Y may be preferable if the estimate is relevant, complete and transparently described; estimation uncertainty does not automatically mean error.

practice.prompt: Can information be useful if irrelevant but perfectly accurate?
practice.explanation: Both relevance and faithful representation are fundamental.
Prudence is caution under uncertainty, consistent with neutrality.

practice.answer: Knowledgeable independent observers could reach consensus that the depiction is faithfully represented.
practice.explanation: It does not require one unique estimate.

examTask.prompt: Recommend which measurement to use and discuss two qualitative-characteristic trade-offs.
modelPoints: Start with relevance and faithful representation.
Use enhancing characteristics to compare viable alternatives.
Mention transparent uncertainty and cost where facts support it.

sequence.title: Recognition, derecognition and measurement

syllabus.outcomeReferences: category-level draft; cross-check exact lettering against selected sitting

prerequisites: ACCA FR A1 or equivalent diagnostic
objectives: Apply the asset, liability, income and expense definitions.
Explain recognition as providing relevant and faithfully represented information.
Distinguish historical cost and current-value bases.
Identify when derecognition or continued presentation needs analysis.

workedExample.scenario: An entity pays 120 for a non-refundable right expected to generate benefits and separately faces a probable obligation from past environmental damage.
steps: Identify rights and obligations, not labels.
Assess control/present obligation and past events.
Select a measurement basis consistent with useful information.
workedExample.answer: The purchased right may be an asset if it is a controlled present economic resource. The environmental duty may be a liability if a present obligation exists from the past damage. Recognition and measurement require the relevant IFRS requirements; probability wording alone is not a substitute for those requirements.

practice.prompt: Is physical form required for an asset?
practice.explanation: An asset is a present economic resource, which is a right with potential to produce benefits.
Assess relevance and faithful representation under the applicable Standard.

practice.answer: Fair value, value in use or current cost.
practice.explanation: The exact basis depends on the item and Standard.

examTask.prompt: Analyse two supplied items for element definition, recognition and measurement; state any information still needed.
modelPoints: Do not jump from cash payment to asset.

sequence.title: Regulation, standard setting and ethical reporting judgement

syllabus.outcomeReferences: category-level draft; cross-check exact lettering against selected sitting

prerequisites: ACCA FR A1 or equivalent diagnostic
objectives: Explain why financial reporting is regulated.
Distinguish IFRS Foundation, IASB and jurisdictional adoption/enforcement roles.
Use due-process logic at a high level.
Identify bias, omission and pressure risks in an accounting judgement.

workedExample.scenario: A manager asks the reporting team to defer a known impairment review until after a financing meeting.
steps: Identify the applicable reporting requirement and reporting-period facts.
Document evidence, escalate appropriately and keep the conclusion independent.
workedExample.answer: Financing pressure does not change the reporting requirement. The team should perform the required assessment using reporting-date evidence, document the judgement, and use governance/escalation routes if management pressure threatens faithful reporting.

practice.prompt: Does IASB enforce every company's statements?
practice.explanation: IASB issues IFRS Accounting Standards; adoption and enforcement involve jurisdictions and regulators.

practice.answer: To support transparent, consultative and evidence-informed standard setting.

practice.prompt: What is the first response to pressure to omit evidence?
practice.answer: Preserve and assess the evidence under the requirement.
practice.explanation: Then document and escalate through appropriate governance.

examTask.prompt: Discuss the reporting and ethical issues in the financing-pressure scenario and recommend actions.
modelPoints: Give proportionate documentation and escalation steps.

sequence.title: Property, plant and equipment: initial and subsequent measurement

syllabus.outcomeReferences: category-level draft; cross-check exact lettering against selected sitting

prerequisites: ACCA FR A1 or equivalent diagnostic
objectives: Identify directly attributable costs at initial recognition.
Exclude operating losses and abnormal waste from asset cost.
Calculate depreciation from the available-for-use date.
Account for a revaluation movement at a foundation level.

workedExample.scenario: Machine price 500; delivery 20; installation 30; staff training 12; abnormal testing waste 8; residual value 50; useful life 10 years; available for use on 1 April.
workedExample.answer: Capitalise price, delivery and installation: 550. Expense training and abnormal waste: 20. Full-year depreciation is 50; charge from 1 April using the entity's time-apportionment policy.

practice.explanation: 500 + 20 + 30; training and abnormal waste are excluded.

practice.answer: When the asset is available for use.
practice.explanation: Not automatically on invoice or payment date.

examTask.prompt: Prepare the PPE calculation and explain treatment of each cost plus the depreciation commencement date.
modelPoints: Use depreciable amount, not gross cost.
State time apportionment from available-for-use date.

sequence.title: Intangible assets and development expenditure

syllabus.outcomeReferences: category-level draft; cross-check exact lettering against selected sitting

prerequisites: ACCA FR A1 or equivalent diagnostic
objectives: Distinguish research from development expenditure.
Apply the development-capitalisation criteria as a complete set.
Explain finite versus indefinite useful life treatment.
Avoid recognising internally generated brands and similar items when prohibited.

workedExample.scenario: Research phase costs 90. From 1 July all development criteria are demonstrated; later eligible costs are 240. Product available for use 1 October with five-year life.
workedExample.answer: Expense 90 research. Capitalise only the 240 incurred after all criteria are demonstrated. Annual amortisation is 48 and three months from availability is 12.

practice.prompt: Can later success reinstate earlier research cost?
practice.explanation: Previously expensed research is not reinstated.

examTask.prompt: Calculate the amounts in profit or loss and financial position and explain the recognition cut-off.
modelPoints: Capitalise only after every criterion is met.
